calls.body: The Stars’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Blue Jackets’ kill is one of the worst. Every trip to the box hurts the Blue Jackets more than most.

calls.head: Crash the net vs. Bombs away
calls.body: The Stars get in close, but the Blue Jackets mostly shoot from distance. Dallas is one of the league’s best for shots from in close, and Columbus is near the bottom. Shots from in close tend to be more dangerous, so expect the Stars to do more of their damage around the net.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Stars get past the Blue Jackets
paras: Mikko Rantanen got the scoring started for the Stars on the power play early in the first. Thomas Harley made it 2-0 with just one second left in the period, and that one stood up as the winner. The Blue Jackets’ Erik Gudbranson didn’t play after 16:38 of the second period. Columbus had a goal taken off for offside early in the third. Damon Severson cut Dallas’ lead to 2-1 early in the period, and Arttu Hyry shut the door with an empty-netter with just one second left.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Jake Oettinger made 24 saves for the Stars, and Jet Greaves stopped 14 of 16 at the other end. The Stars improved to 8-5-1, fourth in the Central, while the Blue Jackets dropped to 5-7-0, seventh in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Thomas Harley scored his first goal of the season, his first since Mar 14 (29 games played since).
The Stars’ Esa Lindell was back in the lineup after missing five games.
The Stars’ David Perron played his first game of the season, after missing the first 13.
The Stars bounced back after two straight losses.
